the reference's embedded chroma XML lexers. Recover them with devutils/embedextract: `go build -o /tmp/embedextract ./devutils/embedextract` then `/tmp/embedextract -bin ~/.local/bin/agy -embed-out <dir>` writes the //go:embed file systems; the 279 files under its 'embedded/' root are upstream chroma's lexers/embedded/*.xml, and the 74 at the root are upstream's styles/*.xml. Each line here is '<file base> <the alias that lexer registers>'. Verified at 1.5.15, 1.5.16 and 1.5.17: all 353 embedded XML files in out/extracted-1.5.17/embed are byte-identical to 1.5.14 / upstream chroma v2.27.0, so a changed file set at a new release means the reference's chroma moved and the clone's dependency pin must follow it - see docs/cycles/cycle-300-chroma-parity/deliverable.md

run the real agy with CLOUD_CODE_URL pointed at devutils/refcapture, a mock that forwards every RPC except streamGenerateContent to the real CloudCode endpoint, answers the agent turn with one functionCall, and then reads functionResponse.response.output in the follow-up request the reference sends. The forwarding is load-bearing: at 1.4.7 the reference runs an eligibility check against loadCodeAssist before the first turn, and a stubbed response cannot satisfy it. Drive it in print mode (agy -p) with --dangerously-skip-permissions and the workspace at /tmp; the view_file / generate_image / read_url_content sections need a custom agent (a workspace .agents/agents/test.md plus --agent test). the tool names agy knows, read out of the binary: a []string global whose backing array sits at file offset 0xb623bb0 (vmaddr 0x10b623bb0), whose slice header sits at 0xb5ba450 and whose length is 63. The names are sorted here because the reference sorts them before it writes init.tools. This is the reference's *known* set, not what it advertises: a live session's init.tools holds 60 of the 63 - the three searches (code_search, moma_search, skill_search) are withheld. Re-verify by reading the slice out of ~/.local/bin/agy (sha256 09fcdd8554e03bed9b2ec936e454c7f115d5610610de09ed7d79fa2feae76940) and decoding the 63 string headers

the reference's own per-tool descriptions, read out of agy (~/.local/bin/agy, sha256 09fcdd8554e03bed9b2ec936e454c7f115d5610610de09ed7d79fa2feae76940). The binary has three tool surfaces: the advertised list (names only), the converter layer (cortex/tools/*, gemini_coder/framework/toolconverters - the prose that assembles a tool definition) and the runtime layer (cortex/core/tools/tools, oneharness/internal/app/tools/tools - the Description() methods, twelve of which are the declarations the reference sends to the model). Thirty-seven of the sixty-three advertised names carry text - the thirty-seventh is browser_subagent, whose text lives in the binary's built-in agents package (cortex/customizations/builtin/agents) rather than in a tool layer; 'layer' records which surface each text came from, 'complete' is false for run_workflow (fragments only). run_command's 'text' is the reference's converter template with the operating system, the shell and the two prose parts substituted - the darwin rendering - and its 'model_facing' field holds the runtime text the reference's declaration carries. Every literal (or its fragment) is still present in the 1.4.8 binary, byte for byte. Re-verify by reading the literals out of the binary at the addresses the report gives

the reference's second set of model-facing tool texts. agy 1.4.8 holds two variants of four descriptions (run_command, send_message, manage_subagents, edit_file); the default - the one a live session sends - is what internal/app/tools/surface/model_tools_1.4.6.json carries, and the alternates are recorded here with the vmaddr/length of every literal they are built from. The selection between the two is runtime/flag dependent and was not traced, so the clone ships the default. Every address in the file was re-derived against agy 1.4.8 in cycle 359; the texts themselves are byte-identical to the 1.4.7 capture, only their addresses moved. Re-verify by reading the literals out of ~/.local/bin/agy (sha256 09fcdd8554e03bed9b2ec936e454c7f115d5610610de09ed7d79fa2feae76940) at the addresses the file gives
